text: Bush was the Chairman of a task force on international terrorism which issued a report shortly before that decision was made and said, and rightly so, that we never ever can make concessions to terrorists and hostage takers.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And, yet, after sitting through meeting after meeting, he endorsed that decision, endorsed the sale of arms to the Ayatollah in exchange for hostages, one of the most tragic, one of the most mistaken foreign policy decisions we’ve ever made in this country and I dare say encouraged others to take hostages as we now know.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: So, there can be no concessions under any circumstances, because if we do it’s an open invitation to others to do the same.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We’ve got to be tough on international terrorism.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We’ve got to treat it as international crime.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We’ve got to attack at all points, we’ve go to use undercover operations.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We have to be prepared to use military force against terrorist base camps, we have to work closely with our allies to make sure that they’re working with us and we with them and we can give no quarter when it comes to breaking the back of international terrorism.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Yes, we should make every effort to try to help those hostages come home, but it can never be because we make concessions.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: That was a tragic mistake that we made, a mistake that Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Bush made and others made and it should never ever be made again.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Mr.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President?

speaker: BUSH
text: I wrote the anti-terrorist report for this government.

speaker: BUSH
text: It is the best anti-terrorist report written.

speaker: BUSH
text: Yes, we shouldn’t trade arms for hostages.

speaker: BUSH
text: But we have made vast improvements in our anti-terrorism.

speaker: BUSH
text: Now, it’s fine to say that sometimes you have to hit base camps, but when the president saw this state sponsored-fingerprints of Muammar Khadaffi on the loss of American life, he hit Libya.

speaker: BUSH
text: And my opponent was unwilling to support that action.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: That’s not true.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: That’s not true.

speaker: BUSH
text: And since that action, terrorist action against the United States citizens have gone down.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: That’s not true.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I have long ago said I supported the president on this other matter.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I’ve said mistakes were made.

speaker: BUSH
text: Clearly nobody’s going to think the president started out thinking he was going to trade arms for hostages.

speaker: BUSH
text: That is a very serious charge against the president.

speaker: BUSH
text: The matter has been thoroughly looked into.

speaker: BUSH
text: But the point is sometimes the action-

speaker: BUSH
text: – has to be taken by the Federal Government and when we took action, it had a favorable response.

speaker: LEHRER
text: A question for the Vice President.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Peter?

speaker: JENNINGS
text: It seems perhaps a good subject, Mr.

speaker: JENNINGS
text: Vice President, on which to make the point that you’ve campaigned vigorously as part of a leadership team.

speaker: JENNINGS
text: But so far you won’t tell the American people in considerable measure what advice you gave the president, including the sale of arms to Iran and what should have been done about the hostages.

speaker: JENNINGS
text: To the best of my knowledge there’s no Constitutional requirement which prevents you from doing so.

speaker: JENNINGS
text: Jimmy Carter urged his Vice President, Walter Mondale, to tell the American people.

speaker: JENNINGS
text: Would you now ask President Reagan for permission to tell the American people what advice you did give him?

speaker: JENNINGS
text: And if you don’t, how do we judge your judgment in the Oval Office in the last eight years?

speaker: BUSH
text: You’re judged by the whole record.

speaker: BUSH
text: You’re judged by the entire record.

speaker: BUSH
text: Are we closer to peace?

speaker: BUSH
text: Are we doing better in anti-terrorism?

speaker: BUSH
text: Should we have listened to my opponent who wanted to send the UN into the Persian Gulf or in spite of the mistakes of the past, are we doing better there?

speaker: BUSH
text: How is our credibility with the GCC countries on the Western side of the Gulf.

speaker: BUSH
text: Is Iran talking to Iraq about peace?

speaker: BUSH
text: You judge on the record.

speaker: BUSH
text: Are the Soviets coming out of Afghanistan?

speaker: BUSH
text: How does it look in a program he called or some one of these marvelous Boston adjective up there and-about Angola-now, we have a chance-several Bostonians don’t like it, but the rest of the country will understand.

speaker: BUSH
text: Now we have a chance.

speaker: BUSH
text: Now we have a chance.

speaker: BUSH
text: And, so, I think that I’d leave it right there and say that you judge on the whole record.

speaker: BUSH
text: And let me say this-all he can talk about-he goes around ranting about Noriega.

speaker: BUSH
text: Now, I’ve told you what the intelligence briefing he received said about that.

speaker: BUSH
text: He can talk about Iran/Contra and also-I’ll make a deal with you, I will take the blame for those two incidents if you give me half the credit for all the good things that have happened in world peace since Ronald Reagan and I took over from the Carter administration.

speaker: BUSH
text: I still have a couple of minutes left.

speaker: BUSH
text: And there is a difference principle –

speaker: LEHRER
text: Sorry, Mr.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President.

speaker: BUSH
text: It’s only on yellow here.

speaker: BUSH
text: Wait a minute.

speaker: LEHRER
text: I’m wrong.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Go ahead.

speaker: LEHRER
text: My apologies.

speaker: BUSH
text: Jim –

speaker: LEHRER
text: You said nobody’s perfect.

speaker: BUSH
text: I said I wasn’t perfect.

speaker: BUSH
text: Where was I?

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: 25th of December, Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Vice President.

speaker: BUSH
text: I finished.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: He can have another ten seconds if he wants, Jim.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Governor, you have a minute to respond.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Well, the matter of judgment is very important.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And I think it’s important to understand what happened here.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: A report on international terrorism chaired by the Vice President was released and made some very specific recommendations about how to deal with terrorism.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: They were ignored.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: The Vice President ignored them.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: He says mistakes were made.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Very serious mistakes in judgment were made.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: He says, â‰¥Well, let’s concede that the administration has been doing business with Noriega.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Has made him a part of our foreign policy and has been funneling aid to Contras through convicted drug dealers.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: â‰¤ I think those are very very serious questions of judgment, which those of you who are watching us here tonight have a right to judge and review.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We’re not going to make those kinds of mistakes.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: You cannot make concessions to terrorists.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: If you do, you invite the taking of more hostages.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: That’s a basic principle.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: It was ignored in that case and it was a very very serious mistake in judgment.

speaker: LEHRER
text: A question from John Mashek.

speaker: LEHRER
text: It goes to the Vice President.

speaker: MASHEK
text: Mr.

speaker: MASHEK
text: Vice President, Democrats and even some Republicans are still expressing reservations about the qualifications and credentials of Senator Dan Quayle of Indiana, your chosen running mate, to be a heartbeat away from the presidency.

speaker: MASHEK
text: What do you see in him that others do not?

speaker: BUSH
text: I see a young man that was elected to the Senate twice, to the House of Representatives twice.

speaker: BUSH
text: I see a man who is young and I am putting my confidence in a whole generation of people that are in their 30Ï€s and 40Ï€s.

speaker: BUSH
text: I see a man that took the leadership in the Job Training Partnership Act and that retrains people in this highly competitive changing society we’re in, so if a person loses his hob he is retrained for a benefit-for a-work that will be productive and he won’t have to go on one of these many programs that the liberal-talking about.

speaker: BUSH
text: I see a young man who is a knowledgeable-in defense and there are three people on our ticket that are knowledgeable-in the whole-in the race-knowledgeable in defense and Dan Quayle is one of them and I am one of them.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I believe that he will be outstanding.

speaker: BUSH
text: And he took a tremendous pounding and everybody now knows that he took a very unfair pounding.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I’d like each person to say did I jump to conclusions running down rumors that were so outrageous and so brutal.

speaker: BUSH
text: And he’s kept his head up.

speaker: BUSH
text: And he will do very very well.

speaker: BUSH
text: And he has my full confidence and he’ll have the confidence of people that are in their 30Ï€s and 40Ï€s and more.

speaker: BUSH
text: So, judge the man on his record not on the-lot of rumors and innuendo and trying to fool around with his name.

speaker: BUSH
text: My opponent says J.

speaker: BUSH
text: Danforth Quayle.

speaker: BUSH
text: Do you know who J.

speaker: BUSH
text: Danforth was, he was a man who gave his life in World War II, so ridiculing a person’s name is a little beneath this process.

speaker: BUSH
text: And he’ll do very well when we get into the debates.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Well, when it comes to ridicule, George, you win a gold medal.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I think we can agree on that in the course of this campaign.

speaker: BUSH
text: Just the facts.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: But did I-did I sense a desire that maybe Lloyd Bentsen ought to be your running mate when you said there are three people on your ticket?

speaker: BUSH
text: No, I think the debate ought to be between you and Lloyd.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I think the American people have a right to judge us on this question, on how we picked a running mate, a person who is a heartbeat away from the presidency.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I picked Lloyd Bentsen, distinguished, strong, mature, a leader in the Senate, somebody whose qualifications nobody has questioned.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Bush picked Dan Quayle.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I doubt very much that Dan Quayle was the best qualified person for that job.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And as a matter of fact, I think for most people the notion of President Quayle is a very very troubling thought.

speaker: LEHRER
text: John will ask a question of the Governor.

speaker: LEHRER
text: It will be the last question and then the Vice President will have a rebuttal.

speaker: MASHEK
text: Well, Governor, you did select Lloyd Bentsen of Texas.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I did indeed.

speaker: MASHEK
text: And you have a lot of disagreement with him on fundamental issues, including the Reagan tax cuts, aid to the rebels in Nicaragua, the death penalty, gun control.

speaker: MASHEK
text: Who’s right?

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Well, John, I’m a man that’s been a chief executive for ten years.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I’ve picked a lot of people.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I’ve picked cabinets.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I’ve named judges.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I know that the people you pick make an enormous difference in your ability to govern and I set high standards.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I try to meet them and I insist that people who work for me meet them, if they don’t, they don’t stick around very long.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: But I didn’t pick Lloyd Bentsen because he was a clone of Mike Dukakis.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I picked him because he was somebody who would be a strong Vice President, somebody who would be an active Vice President.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Somebody who would come to me if somebody came up with a crazy idea that we ought to trade arms to the Ayatollah for hostages and say, â‰¥Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: President, that’s wrong.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We shouldn’t do that.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: â‰¤ That’s the kind of Vice President I want.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: He, himself, has said, and rightly so, that he’ll be a strong Vice President.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: When the Vice President makes a decision, that will be his decision.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And I’m very very proud of that choice.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And I didn’t pick him because he agreed with me on everything.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: You know, Sam Rayburn once said that if two people agree on everything then only one person is doing the thinking.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: The fact is I’ve picked somebody who not only will be a great Vice President, but if, God forbid, something happens to the president, could step into that office and do so with distinction and with strength and with leadership.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I doubt very much.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I doubt very much that Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Bush’s selection for the Vice Presidency of the United States meets that test.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Mr.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President?

speaker: BUSH
text: Well, I-we obviously have a difference.

speaker: BUSH
text: I believe it does meet the test.

speaker: BUSH
text: We’ll have an opportunity to see the two of them in action in a friendly forum, wonderful friendly fashion like this.

speaker: BUSH
text: I had hoped this had been a little friendlier evening.

speaker: BUSH
text: I wanted to hitchhike a ride home in his tank with him.

speaker: BUSH
text: But now we’ve got the lines too carefully drawn here.

speaker: BUSH
text: But you talk about judgment.

speaker: BUSH
text: I mean, what kind of judgment-I mean, jumping all over the president on his decision on one area of farm policy.

speaker: BUSH
text: What kind of judgment sense has your chief education adviser now in jail in Massachusetts?

speaker: BUSH
text: I mean, there’s-I don’t think this is a fair argument.

speaker: BUSH
text: But nevertheless, I support my nominee for Vice President and he’ll do an outstanding job.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Gentlemen, I was given some bad word a moment ago.

speaker: LEHRER
text: There is time for one more question.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Getting it in my ear and Ann Groer will ask it.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Ann?

speaker: LEHRER
text: To the Governor.

speaker: GROER
text: Governor Dukakis, as many U.

speaker: GROER
text: farmers face or undergo foreclosure, the United States is considering the possibility of forgiving a certain percentage of debt owed by Latin American and Third World countries, do you favor giving these countries a break in their loans and, if so, how do you explain that to the American farmers who are losing their land and livelihood?

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Well, I think we have to go to work on the problem of Third World debt and we’ve got to assist those Third World countries in dealing with this massive debt which they currently-which they have incurred and which is burdening them and which if we don’t do something about it and assist them along with other nations around the world, we’ll destroy their economies, destroy their future.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And at the same time will destroy markets that are important to our farmers.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: But I also believe we need an agricultural policy which doesn’t cost us 15 to 20 to 25 billion dollars a year that it’s been costing us over the course of the past three or four years under this administration.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I think it’s going to require good, solid credit policies.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And thanks to the Congress we now have an agricultural credit bill which is helping and improving the situation with at least some of our farmers.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I think it’s going to require a combination of supply management and reasonable price supports to make sure that our farmers get a decent price and I think it also is going to require an administration that understand that there are tremendous opportunities out there for the development of new uses for agricultural products, new uses which can help us to clean up our environment at the same time.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Bio-degradable plastics-plastic-gasohol, which the Vice President has been involved in, road de-icers made from corn products.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I mean, there are enormous opportunities out there to expand markets and to build a strong future for our farmers.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: But I don’t think there’s anything mutually exclusive or contradictory about building a strong farm economy in this country and assisting our family farms and providing a good strong future for rural communities and for rural America and at the same time working on Third World debt.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: As a matter of fact, Mexico, itself, is one of our biggest agricultural customers, so in the sense that we can work to help Mexico rebuild and expand and deal with these very serious economic problems we help our farmers at the same time.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Mr.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President?

speaker: BUSH
text: I oppose supply management and production controls.

speaker: BUSH
text: I support the farm bill, the 1985 farm bill and spending is moving in the right direction.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to expand our markets abroad and that’s why I’ve called for that first economic summit to be on agriculture.

speaker: BUSH
text: I will not go back to the way the Democrats did it and used food as a political weapon and throw a grain embargo on the farmers in this country.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to see rural redevelopment and I have been out front in favor of alternate sources of energy and one of them is gasohol and comes from using your corn and I think we can do better in terms of biodegradable for a lot of product, so I’m optimistic about the agricultural economy.

speaker: BUSH
text: In terms of the Third World, I support the Baker plan.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to see market economies spring up all around the world and to the degree they do, we are succeeding.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I don’t want to see the banks let off the hook.

speaker: BUSH
text: I would oppose that, but I think were on the right track in agriculture and I am very very encouraged.

speaker: BUSH
text: But let’s not go back to that-what they call supply management and production control, that’ll simply price us out of the international market.

speaker: BUSH
text: Let’s try to expand our markets abroad.

speaker: LEHRER
text: All right.

speaker: LEHRER
text: That really is the end.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Now, let’s go to closing statements.

speaker: LEHRER
text: They will be two minutes each in duration by agreement.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President Bush goes first.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Governor Dukakis second.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Mr.

speaker: LEHRER
text: Vice President.

speaker: BUSH
text: I talked in New Orleans about a gentler and kinder nation and I have made specific proposals on education and the environment and on ethics and energy and how we do better in battling crime in our country.

speaker: BUSH
text: But there are two main focal points of this election.

speaker: BUSH
text: Opportunity and peace.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to keep this expansion going.

speaker: BUSH
text: Yes, we want change but we are the change.

speaker: BUSH
text: I am the change.

speaker: BUSH
text: I don’t want to go back to malaise and misery index.

speaker: BUSH
text: And, so, opportunity.

speaker: BUSH
text: Keep America at work.

speaker: BUSH
text: The best poverty program is a job with dignity in the private sector.

speaker: BUSH
text: And in terms of peace, we are on the right track.

speaker: BUSH
text: We’ve achieved an arms control agreement that our critics thought was never possible and I want to build on it.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to see us finalize that START agreement and I want it to be the one to finally lead the world to banishing chemical and biological weapons.

speaker: BUSH
text: I want to see asymmetrical reductions in conventional forces.

speaker: BUSH
text: And then it gets down to a question of values.

speaker: BUSH
text: We’ve had a chance to spell out our differences on the Pledge of Allegiance here tonight and on tough sentencing of drug king pins and this kind of thing.

speaker: BUSH
text: And I do favor the death penalty.

speaker: BUSH
text: And we’ve got a wide array of differences on those.

speaker: BUSH
text: But in the final analysis-in the final analysis, the person goes into that voting booth, they’re going to say, â‰¥Who has the values I believe in?

speaker: BUSH
text: Who has the experience that we trust?

speaker: BUSH
text: Who has the integrity and stability to get the job done?

speaker: BUSH
text: â‰¤ My fellow Americans, I am that man and I ask for your support.

speaker: BUSH
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: This has been an extraordinary 18 months for Kitty and me and for our family.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We’ve had an opportunity to campaign all over this country and to meet with so many of you in communities and states and regions to get to know you.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I’m more optimistic today than I was when I began about this nation providing we have the kind of leadership in Washington that can work with you, that can build partnerships, that can build jobs in every part of this country, not certain parts of this country.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: You know, my friends, my parents came to this country as immigrants like millions and millions of Americans before them and since, seeking opportunities, seeking the American dream.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: They made sure their sons understood that this was the greatest country in the world, that those of us especially who were the sons and daughters of immigrants had a special responsibility to give something to the country that had opened up its arms to our parents and given so much to them.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I believe in the American dream.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: I’m a product of it and I want to help that dream come true for every single citizen in this land, with a good job and good wages, with good schools in every part of this country and every community in this country.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: With decent and affordable housing that our people can buy and own and live in, so that we end the shame of hopelessness in America.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: With decent and affordable healthcare for all working families.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Yes, it’s a tough problem as Mr.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Bush says, but itÏ€s not an insolvable problem.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: It’s one that we will solve and must solve, with a clean and wholesome environment and with a strong America that’s strong militarily and economically as we must be, an America that provides strong international leadership because we’re true to our values.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We have an opportunity working together to build that future, to build a better America, to build a best America, because the best America doesn’t hide.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We compete.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: The best America.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We invest.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: The best America doesn’t leave some of its citizens behind.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: We live-we bring everybody along.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: And the best America is not behind us.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: The best America is yet to come.

speaker: DUKAKIS
text: Thank you very much.
